key_insight: LoMeVQA shows that current multimodal models still struggle with temporal reasoning in longitudinal medical imaging, even when they are strong on standard VQA tasks.
clinical_relevance: Better modeling of disease change across visits could improve assessment of progression and treatment response in routine imaging workflows.
method: Built LoMeVQA with 206K longitudinal VQA pairs for five tasks.
Used an automated pipeline to order patient records, extract entities with a medical knowledge graph, and model temporal evolution.
Introduced MedLong-8B and evaluated general-purpose vs. medical-domain MLLMs on longitudinal reasoning.
evidence_signal: The benchmark evaluations found that both general and medical MLLMs performed poorly on LoMeVQA, while MedLong-8B achieved state-of-the-art results across all tasks.
watch_item: Performance on a synthetic or pipeline-generated benchmark may not fully capture real-world clinical variability, so external validation is still needed.
paper_title: LoMeVQA: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Longitudinal Medical VQA
